sections.skill: Estimate self-employment and income taxes for a small business and plan quarterly payments

questions.prompt: Dev's T-shirt business earns $28,000 in sales with $8,000 of business expenses. What is his net profit for taxes?
questions.intro: Self-employed people report business income and expenses (on Schedule C). Net profit = income − deductible business expenses. Taxes are figured on net profit.
sources: IRS (Self-employment tax): Self-employment tax is 15.3% (12.4% Social Security and 2.9% Medicare) and is figured on 92.35% of net earnings from self-employment; it applies when net earnings are $400 or more. (https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/self-employment-tax-social-security-and-medicare-taxes)

IRS (Estimated taxes): People who expect to owe $1,000 or more when they file, such as many self-employed workers, generally must pay estimated tax quarterly. (https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/estimated-taxes)

questions.prompt: Self-employment tax is 15.3% of 92.35% of net profit. On $20,000 of net profit, what is it?
questions.intro: Employees pay 7.65% for Social Security and Medicare, and employers pay another 7.65%. Self-employed people pay both halves: 15.3%, figured on 92.35% of net earnings.
sources: IRS (Self-employment tax): Self-employment tax is 15.3% (12.4% Social Security and 2.9% Medicare) and is figured on 92.35% of net earnings from self-employment; it applies when net earnings are $400 or more. (https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/self-employment-tax-social-security-and-medicare-taxes)

IRS (Estimated taxes): People who expect to owe $1,000 or more when they file, such as many self-employed workers, generally must pay estimated tax quarterly. (https://www.irs.gov/businesses/small-businesses-self-employed/estimated-taxes)

questions.prompt: Why do many self-employed people pay estimated taxes four times a year?

choices.text: The IRS charges a fee for filing once a year
They pay no tax at the end of the year
No employer withholds tax from their pay

questions.correct_answer: No employer withholds tax from their pay
questions.intro: If you expect to owe $1,000 or more when you file, the IRS generally requires quarterly estimated payments. Missing them can cause penalties.
questions.feedback: Without withholding, self-employed people pay as they go through estimated taxes.
